explanations.text:
●  the page loads the project                           ([script](script))
│     The page asks for one record, human.json, that names the files
│     of the project. For every file it then asks for the record of
│     its abstractions, explanation_<name>.json in the map folder. A
│     file with no record gets an empty one, so the page still shows
│     it. The file itself comes only when you open the file. The
│     human.json is always in the list, first, under the name
│     human/human.json. It also asks for project.json, the record
│     about the project as a whole; when it holds abstractions it
│     joins the list too, under the name human/project.json.
│
●  the page draws the file tree                             ([main](main))
│     On the left: the project name and its files. A click on a
│     file opens that file.
│
●  the page opens one file                                  ([open](open))
│     It keeps the lines of the file and every abstraction, and it
│     remembers which piece of the file each abstraction is about.
│     It also remembers which abstractions you left open, so a file
│     you come back to opens as you left it. A writing box left open
│     closes when you go to another file.
│
●  the page puts the abstractions in order               ([sorted](sorted))
│     A pin points from one abstraction at another. The abstraction
│     nobody points at is the most abstract, and it goes last. An
│     abstraction that a pin points at goes above the one that holds
│     the pin, and so on upward. Among equals, the one about earlier
│     lines goes first.
│
●  the page draws the list                              ([render](render))
│     Every abstraction is one header line: a small arrow, the name
│     of its piece, its lines, and a write link on the right. All
│     start folded the first time. Under the header the words are
│     drawn exactly as written. A pin whose target has an abstraction
│     is lit; a pin with none is muted. The bar on top says how many
│     are open. The project map carries a link for a new abstraction
│     on top; a file with no map offers to write a telling for it, or
│     to write the code itself. Only human.json takes no writing.
│     An entry whose writing waits for claude is marked compiling,
│     with a count when more than one waits.
│
●  you write                                          ([the box](startEdit))
│     A click on write puts a box in the place of the words. It holds
│     the text as it is in the map — the pins in their brackets, the
│     targets visible — or the code of the file, or nothing for a new
│     abstraction. What you type stays in the browser until you send
│     it, so a box you come back to holds what you left; cancel
│     [closes it and forgets the draft](stopEdit).
│
●  you press compile and the server answers            ([compile](compile))
│     The box goes to the server, which runs the command you would
│     have typed. A refusal comes back in the command's own words,
│     in the warning colour, and your words stay in the box. A pass
│     redraws the page with [the map read again](reloadMap) and says
│     which writing now waits for claude.
│
●  the page watches the queue                         ([pollQueue](pollQueue))
│     Every three seconds it asks the server what still waits and
│     marks the entries. When claude finishes, the mark goes.
│
●  you click                                                ([jump](jump))
│     A click on a header folds or unfolds that abstraction.
│     A click on a lit pin scrolls to the abstraction it points at,
│     unfolds it, and lights it for a moment.
│
●  you cross to another file                      ([crossJump](crossJump))
      A pin can name a file of the project instead of a piece of
      this one. A click on it opens that file and goes to the piece
      the pin names. A pin to a file the project does not hold, or
      to a piece with no abstraction, is muted and shows the piece
      name. A pin can also name one abstraction of that file and
      words inside it: a click opens the file, goes to that
      abstraction, and lights those words for a moment. Such a pin
      to words the abstraction does not hold is muted and shows the
      file and the number of the abstraction; when the file holds no
      such abstraction at all, a line on top says so.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  the look of the page                                    ([style](style))
     Two panes on a quiet ground: the tree on the left, the reader on
     the right. Text in a typewriter face, so drawings keep their
     columns. A dark and a light version, chosen by your system. On a
     narrow screen the tree hides and slides in over the reader. The
     writing box keeps the typewriter face and can be pulled taller.

  small helpers
     makes text safe to show on a page                        ([esc](esc))
     shows one line when there is nothing to read              ([msg](msg))
     opens and hides the tree on a narrow screen        ([drawer](drawer))
     builds the file tree for one project         ([buildTree](buildTree))
     asks for the file when you open it             ([loadCode](loadCode))
     finds a file of the project by name                ([fileOf](fileOf))
     says if a piece has an abstraction         ([crossEntry](crossEntry))
     says if an abstraction has those words   ([crossAnchor](crossAnchor))
     finds which abstraction a pin points at        ([targetOf](targetOf))
     turns the pins of one line into links          ([lineHtml](lineHtml))
     says the name the server knows a file by       ([nameOf](nameOf))
     names where a draft is kept in the browser     ([draftKey](draftKey))
     marks what still waits for claude          ([queuedMark](queuedMark))
     draws the writing box                      ([editorHtml](editorHtml))
     lights the words a pin points at         ([flashAnchor](flashAnchor))
